04aa40
  • Games: 10 slots (More → 💾 Saved games). The game in progress saves itself to its slot every year and when you leave the app; «Save now» forces a save. 📤 copies a game as text so you can move it to another phone or computer.
  • Difficulty: 🌱 Easy (+12 points on every roll, +15% income, −10% expenses, fewer wars against your country, hints on), ⚖️ Medium (calibrated with real data) and 🔥 Hard (−10 points, −10% income, +10% expenses, more aggressive AI). Change it in Settings.
  • Themes: Night, Sporty, Corporate, Friendly, Retro, Medieval and Dynamic (Settings → Theme).
  • View: automatic (when you rotate the phone the landscape layout is used: big map on the left and screens on the right), always portrait or always landscape.

4fbd3f
  • The world runs by the hour: the time appears next to the date (a.m. / p.m.) and the map and your scene get dark at night.
  • Every action shows two costs: ⏳ days of your free time for the year (the consistency that habit demands) and 🕗 the hours it takes today. If an action crosses midnight, the world advances one day.
  • By time of day: 🌅 from 5 to 9 a.m. you can go for a sunrise run; the doctor sees patients from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.; 🌙 from 7 p.m. to 3 a.m. you can go out at night (fun, contacts, dating… and some risk); looking for a partner works better at night; studying in the small hours costs concentration.
  • Sleep: from 8 p.m. you can sleep until 7 a.m. If you stay awake past midnight you become sleep-deprived: you lose health and mood every night in a row until you sleep. During the day there is only a nap.
  • With the Hour unit the clock advances hour by hour; Day, Week, Month and Year keep the current time.

a04705 The bottom bar (Actions, Career, advance, Nation, More) is always visible, even with a screen open: the highlighted button shows which section you are in; tap it again to close. Tap any ⓘ or an underlined label to see what it is in the real world and what it does in the game. You can also press and hold any tab or button. You can hide them in Settings.

eab09d Three kinds of game: Hybrid (from person to ruler), Life (person only; the AI runs the country) and Leader (you start as head of state). Clock: advances by Day, Week, Month, Year or 5 years; it stops by itself before important decisions. You live a life year by year in the real world of 2026 (175 countries, ~3,400 provinces, data from the World Bank, IMF, ILO, WHO and SIPRI). Every time you tap +1 YEAR you age, the world moves on (economy, elections, wars all over the world month by month) and events with decisions may appear.
  • 👤 Character view: your life: studies, work, money, family, health, ambition.
  • 🏛️ Country view: when you rule, you run the nation: provinces, army, economy, diplomacy and war.
  • Both views share the same game: you can start as a baby and end up ruling an empire.

f84b94 Every action costs days of your free time (120 a year; ~10 come back each month): studying ~30 days, gym ~20, a date ~5, networking ~10, a campaign ~45. Repeating the same action within the year yields less (diminishing returns). Each one moves your attributes: health, happiness, intelligence, looks and influence.
  • Career: jobs and career paths (politics, military, business, fame). You rise in rank with years of experience, intelligence and influence.
  • Studies: school (grades, clubs), university and graduate degrees; they open better careers.
  • Ambition: you choose a life goal; achieving it gives legacy points.

2dd3f9 Your income uses the real average wage of your region. In Realistic mode there are taxes, inflation, loans, mortgages and bankruptcy.
  • Own business: four types, upgraded by levels; its income depends on the province's economy and on luck.
  • Investments in provinces: “business” (returns ~1.5× the province's growth, with a 4% yearly risk of failure) or “real estate” (follows growth + inflation and pays 3% rent).
  • Fame: streamer, acting, music or sports careers; high fame brings very high income and influence.

451edb Stock market (More → 📈 Stock exchange): 32 real exchanges with their indices (S&P 500, IPC, Ibovespa, DAX, Nikkei…) and more than 100 fictional companies inspired by real ones. Prices move day by day with the clock; when you skip years, the distant past is simulated by weeks and the last six months day by day.
  • Why they move: the country's growth and inflation, central bank rates, wars, recessions, sanctions, coups, currency crises, each company's quarterly results and market sentiment (if valuations inflate, the risk of a crash rises).
  • Charts: candles or line from 1 month to 20 years, moving averages and volume. Tap the chart to see open, high, low and close.
  • Orders: market, limit (highest buy price or lowest sell price) and stop (to cut losses). They expire after 90 trading days. Commission 0.1% (+0.25% if you change currency).
  • Margin and shorts: with a margin account (age 21) you can borrow up to half of what you buy and sell short. If your equity falls below 25% (30% for shorts), there is a margin call and the broker sells for you.
  • Dividends and taxes: dividends are paid every quarter; in Realistic you pay capital gains tax according to your country (Mexico 10%, USA 15%, Switzerland 0%…).
  • Going public: if your business is a large, profitable company, you can sell 20–40% to the public (Assets or Stock market → Portfolio). Its price follows your results; from then on you only collect your share of the profits.
Currencies: your money is in your country's currency (Settings lets you see it in dollars). The exchange rate follows each country's inflation against US inflation plus a deviation driven by interest rates, money printing and crises. If you emigrate or your country is annexed, your savings are converted at that day's rate. Fixed rates can suffer speculative attacks; currencies with high inflation end up removing zeros or changing their name (Iran plans to remove four zeros in 2028).
If you rule (Country → Economy): independent central bank or under your control, policy rate, exchange-rate regime (float, peg, currency board), print money, remove zeros, stabilization plan, dollarize, adopt the euro (if you are in the EU and meet the criteria), leave a monetary union and capital controls.

915101 My companies (More → 🏪): 28 lines of business, from a food stall to a factory, a mine or an oil well. Every month the company sells according to demand (population, economy, tourism, interest rates, reputation, price and marketing), pays for inputs (which follow the price of wheat, corn, coffee, oil, steel, copper or gold), payroll with benefits, rent, interest and the country's real taxes; what it pays out reaches your money.
  • Decisions: price, quality, wages, marketing, payout, employees, branches, loans, putting in or taking out cash, selling, closing or going public.
  • Income statement for the last month, the last 12 months and the previous year, with a sales and profit chart and advice based on what is happening.
  • Bankruptcy: if debts exceed what the company is worth, it closes.
Resources (⛏️ map): 14 commodities with each country's real output spread across its provinces according to terrain. Prices rise when supply is short (wars, occupation, export bans) and fall when the world economy slows; gold rises with fear. They change the growth of exporting countries, world inflation, energy and mining stocks and your companies' costs. Conquering provinces with deposits gives you their output.
Investments (📈 Stock market): index funds, commodities (with storage) and 10-year government bonds (monthly interest, interest-rate and default risk).
If you rule: nationalize or reprivatize oil and mining and ban exports (Country → Economy).

b028e8 Corporate (Career): from Intern to CEO of a company listed on your stock exchange. Executive pay grows with company size. As CEO you make one decision a year (expansion, cuts, buyback, dividend, R&D or acquisition) that moves its stock; if the stock stays below the index for two years, the board fires you.
Finance: from Junior analyst to Chief investment officer at a bank or fund. From Trader on you manage real capital (US$5M to US$1,000M): you split the money among stocks, commodities, currencies and bonds, and the result comes from in-game prices. You get a bonus on profits; if you lose more than 12% in the year, you are fired. You can start your own fund (2% and 20%).
Preparation: MBA (2 years, you join as Manager or Associate), financial analyst certification (3 levels), trading course and management diploma.
Services (More → 🧑‍💼): security, bodyguards, driver, assistant, accountant, lawyer, financial advisor, trainer, nutritionist, chef, household staff and public relations, in three tiers. The risk of kidnapping and extortion depends on your net worth and on your country's real violence.
Ticker bar: below the news; tap it to choose the market (your exchange, Wall Street, world, currencies, commodities) and time frame.
Forex: in Stock market → Currencies you buy and sell currencies; your deposits earn their central bank's rate.
Reserves (Country → Economy): foreign currency, gold and strategic oil; intervene in the exchange rate, buy or sell gold, fill or release the crude reserve.

982d5f Banks (More → 🏦): credit unions, regional and national banks of your country, and international, MEGA and GIGA banks of the world, plus private banking for large fortunes. Small ones pay more interest but fail more often; deposit insurance covers up to 25 average salaries per bank. Your credit history (300–850) sets the rate and amount of your loans.
Funds: money market, conservative, balanced, growth, commodities and hedge; they return what their assets do in the game, minus fees.
Your bank: minimum capital and a license; you set rates, risk and payout; it grows from local to GIGA if you do well, and it can suffer bank runs.
As a country (Country → Economy): regulation, deposit insurance, development banking, World Bank, IMF (in a crisis, with austerity) and nationalizing the banks. Banking crises come when the health of the system falls.
Ministries (Country → Cabinet): 14 ministries with heads of varying competence, honesty and loyalty; if you rule, you appoint them and give directives. As a person you can join the civil service (Career) and become a Minister, also in Life mode: your directives move the country.

6eb3c7 Amateur: train by attribute (power, speed, defense, stamina, chin, technique; in MMA also wrestling and submissions), spar, fight as an amateur and enter tournaments: local, national, continental, world (odd years) and the Olympic Games (every four years). Medals attract promoters.
  • Professional (18+): sign with a promoter (local, national or global) or, in MMA, with a league (regional circuit → Global Fight Arena → World Combat League).
  • The world: each division has generated fighters with nationality, style, attributes, record and potential. They fight each other every month, win and lose belts, retire, and prospects arrive.
  • Sanctioning bodies: CMP, AGB, FIP and OMR (inspired by boxing's big four). Each has its champion and its ranking; whoever holds all four is undisputed champion. The mandatory challenger is the body's number 1.
  • Offers and purses: each offer comes with opponent, rounds, place on the card, venue and purse. You can accept, ask for more (+15%, +35%), a pay-per-view share, a rematch clause or a longer camp. The odds depend on your market value against the opponent's and on your manager; asking too much can kill the fight.
  • Fight week: camp (costs free days), corner team (cutman, strength coach, nutritionist), press conference and weigh-in.
  • The fight: round by round with health, energy, cuts, knockdowns, stats and three judges using the 10-point system. Between rounds you give instructions from the corner. Endings by knockout, technical knockout, submission, unanimous, split or majority decision, or draw.
  • Health: accumulated damage wears down your chin and your health; after a knockout there is a medical suspension. Your trainer and your family will tell you.

2f4310 The world: 12 simulated leagues with fictional clubs in real cities (England, Spain, Italy, Germany, France, Portugal, the Netherlands, Brazil, Argentina, Mexico, USA and Saudi Arabia; plus your country's if you play football). European season (August–May), calendar year, or Apertura and Clausura with playoffs in Mexico. Promotion and relegation, national cups, European Champions League, Champions Cup of the Americas and Club World Cup.
  • National teams: 48-team World Cup (12 groups, best third-placed teams and round of 32) every four years with real hosts (2026 USA/Mexico/Canada, 2030 Spain/Portugal/Morocco, 2034 Saudi Arabia), Euro, Copa América, Gold Cup, Africa Cup and Asian Cup.
  • Your career: position, 7 attributes and an overall that depends on your position; youth academy, debut, role (starter, rotation, substitute), minutes, goals, assists and match rating; form and the coach's trust.
  • Transfers: summer and winter windows, market value, transfer offers, loans, release clause, renewals and free agency. You can negotiate wages and a starting spot.
  • National team: you are called up if your overall approaches the national team's strength. You play FIFA dates and tournaments.
  • Finals: if your club or national team reaches a final, you play it on screen: you decide at the key moments and in the penalty shootout.
  • Awards: top scorer, league player of the year, best young player and Golden Ball.

294f55 One world per career: when you start in music, acting, content creation, modeling, comedy, writing, cooking or as a DJ, its industry is generated: about 60 named figures with country, style, level and audience; fictional companies in four sizes (independent, national, major and multinational); a monthly hit chart, a ranking and a yearly award.
  • Attributes: five per craft, each with a different weight in your level. You practice one at a time and you also learn by working and performing.
  • Works: you choose the type and size of production, work through its sessions (each with variable quality), release it with promotion and get reviews, audience response, a chart position and a month-by-month chart of its life. In acting and modeling you first have to win the audition or casting.
  • Money: as an independent you keep 70% but pay for everything and only reach your own audience. A company gives you an advance, pays for production and brings its reach, in exchange for keeping most of it: your royalties (14–22%) first recoup the advance, and until then you don't get paid.
  • Contracts: offers arrive according to your fame (or knock on doors). You can negotiate advance, royalties, length and creative control with visible odds and a die roll.
  • Live: shows with four decision moments and regional, national, continental and world tours through real cities.
  • Scene: hit chart, ranking, profiles of peers (hang out, collaborate or start a rivalry), award history and news.
  • Awards: five nominees per category; if you are nominated, you live the ceremony: red carpet, envelopes and speech. In cooking, the Gourmet Guide also gives or takes away stars every year.
  • Clock: it stops when an offer, a tour show or a ceremony arrives. In the 5-year fast-forward your team produces, releases, signs and tours for you.

8c3661 How to start: Career → Fame and show business. There are 11 careers: music, acting, football, boxing, MMA, content creator, modeling, comedy, writing, cooking and DJ. Each one uses a key attribute (looks, health or intelligence).
  • Fans by territory: first your province, then your country and finally the world. Each level has a ceiling (its population) and without activity fans drift away.
  • Level and talent: training raises your level; natural talent (×0.7 to ×1.35) multiplies it. The first points come fast and the last ones very slowly.
  • Team: free, regular, professional or elite coach (quality vs. price) and a local, national or international agent (10–20% commission).
  • Contracts: offers arrive every year based on your fame: advance, royalties, length and reach. Scandals can cancel them.
  • Scandals with a cause: provocative posts, statements, canceling due to burnout, or plagiarism. A publicist (Services) reduces the damage; social causes restore your image.
  • Awards and tournaments: Golden Gramophone, Golden Statuette, Golden Pen, Golden Ball, world belts, league titles and the national team.
  • Full time: with no other job or school, every fame activity takes half the days.

68f13c Open More → Dynasty and inheritance.
  • Your children inherit intelligence and looks (the average of you and your partner) and may have a trait: Genius, Athletic, Charismatic, Ambitious, Cunning, Loyal, Sickly or Rebellious.
  • Education: public (free), private or elite: it costs money every year and raises their intelligence.
  • Heir: the eldest by default; you can name someone else.
  • Will: equal split or main heir (70%, plus the house and businesses). The country's real inheritance tax is charged (e.g. USA 40% on anything above ~$14M; Japan 55%; Mexico 0%).
  • Power: in an absolute monarchy or dictatorship the heir inherits the government; if a minor, a regent rules until they turn 18 (and may refuse to hand power back). In a democracy, your political family gives +10 influence.
  • House prestige: adds up each generation's legacy and gives heirs starting influence.

bd8024 Situations don't come from a lottery: they appear because their causes are met (your relationship with someone, your debts, your job, inflation or your country's stability). Every person remembers: relationship, favors they owe you or you owe them, grudges and history; you discover their trait (honest, loyal, generous, ambitious, greedy, vindictive) by dealing with them, and it decides how they respond years later.
  • Options with 🎲 show their chance of success based on your attribute against the difficulty, and the die is visible.
  • Stories continue: a loan gets collected a year later, a bribe can come back as an investigation, a recommendation gets repaid or called in.
  • Good and bad luck are separate, with your country's real probabilities (e.g. the risk of being mugged uses the homicide rate).
  • Settings → frequency: low, normal or high.

449bca
  • Political path: political career, networking and campaigns; elections follow the country's real system (term and re-election).
  • Military path: rise in rank up to General; with influence and a weak regime you can attempt a coup.
  • Inheritance: in absolute monarchies and dictatorships, power passes to your heir.
  • Ruling gives national actions every year, decides wars and opens the 🏛️ Country view.

831746 Tabs of the Country view:
  • Summary: GDP, population, stability, approval, treasury and debt.
  • Provinces: happiness, development, growth and cores. Actions: invest in development, growth program, festival, assimilate or release. Buildings: factory, school, hospital, fortress, port, farm, workshop, library, armory, watchtower and supply depot.
  • Economy: budget in percentages (army, research, welfare…), taxes, bonds and IMF debt, trade treaties, embargoes and technology.
  • Government system: 9 systems (republic, parliamentary monarchy, technocracy, authoritarian republic, absolute monarchy, communism, fascism, theocracy, military junta) with bonuses and penalties; changing system costs stability.
  • Formable nations: 22 historical or regional unions if you control their cores.

901ab0 If you rule or are a General, war is played month by month.
  • Armies: real size; quality depends on spending per soldier; morale, supply and attrition. Tap an army and then a province to move it (it spends the month's movement points).
  • Terrain and winter: mountains, forests, rivers and cold give defense and cause attrition. Defending your own territory gives +20%.
  • Sieges: provinces with a garrison or fortress take months to fall; when they fall they become occupied.
  • Front arrows: every army on the march draws its advance (gold for yours, red for enemies, blue for allies).
  • Resistance: occupied provinces breed guerrillas; when invaded, a country declares general mobilization and forms divisions of conscripts; the aggressor's rival powers may send weapons and volunteers.
  • Peace: the peace conference splits occupied land according to war score. A country capitulates if it loses its capital and more than half its population (or is exhausted); nuclear powers only capitulate if they lose 80%.
  • War weariness: rises with losses and occupation; it lowers stability and pushes toward peace.

d95ce3 Alliances, non-aggression pacts, military access, guarantees, vassals, ultimatums, gifts, insults and calls to arms. Each country's opinion depends on ideology, recent history and your actions. Allies join your wars with their own armies (coalitions).

7e37cd
  • Drag to move around, pinch or use +/− to zoom, ⛶ for full screen.
  • Map modes (icon bar): political, terrain, wealth, population, happiness, development, diplomacy, cores, government, military terrain…
  • Zooming in reveals provinces, more cities, real roads and icons for buildings and ports.
  • Tap a province to see its data and actions.
  • Settings: map effects (water, borders, texture) and roads; More → Light map for slow computers.

0df69b Fast: quick games, fewer penalties and one battle per year outside the Command layer. Realistic: real mortality by age and country, recessions, inflation, taxes and loans, longer and costlier wars.

d09875
  • Invest in education early: intelligence opens almost every career.
  • Have children and choose your heir well: the dynasty is your real long game.
  • Before a war, check the enemy's terrain, winter, supply and alliances.
  • A happy, developed country grows more; conquered provinces without cores rebel.
  • Use ⏩ 5-year fast-forward when there are no important decisions.
